introduction: On this second-last Sunday of the liturgical year, the prophet Malachi announces that for those who fear God, the sun of justice will rise with healing in its rays. In the Gospel, Jesus speaks of the destruction of the temple and of persecutions, and promises that not a hair of our head will perish; by our perseverance we will secure our lives. Paul urges us to work quietly. Let us persevere in faith.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord comes to judge the world with justice. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church in times of trial: that she may persevere in faith and bear witness to Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For Christians persecuted for the name of Jesus: that the Lord may give them words and wisdom. Let us pray to the Lord.
For victims of war, earthquakes, famine and disease: that they may find help and hope. Let us pray to the Lord.
For workers and the unemployed: that all may have dignified work and earn their bread. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that by our perseverance we may secure our lives in God. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, the sun of justice rises with healing for those who fear your name. Keep us steadfast in every trial, and bring us safely to your Kingdom. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: By your endurance
reflection.body:
As the Church's year draws to a close, the readings speak of the end of all things. Malachi describes the day of the Lord as "burning like a furnace" for the proud and the wicked. But for those who fear God, it will be a sunrise: "to you who fear my name shall the sun of righteousness arise with healing in its wings."

In the Gospel, some people are admiring the beauty of the temple in Jerusalem. Jesus tells them that the day will come when "there will not be left here one stone on another that will not be thrown down." This happened in the year 70, when Roman armies destroyed the temple. Nothing on earth is permanent, not even the holiest building.

Jesus warns his followers not to be misled by those who claim to know when the end will come, and not to be terrified by wars and disasters. He tells them plainly that they will be persecuted, even betrayed by their own families. But he promises to be with them: "I will give you a mouth and wisdom which all your adversaries will not be able to withstand." And he gives a promise that seems almost impossible: "not a hair of your head will perish." Then: "By your endurance you will win your lives."

The Christian response to an uncertain future is not panic or speculation, but perseverance: faithfully living each day with our eyes on God.

Paul's advice to the Thessalonians is very practical. Some had stopped working, thinking the end was near. Paul tells them to imitate his example and "work with quietness and eat their own bread." Waiting for the Lord means living responsibly now.

This week, notice what you are anxious about in the world or in your life. Bring it to God, and ask for the grace to persevere, doing your daily work faithfully, with hope.
